title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up a groupoid version of the lemma on the previous page. That lemma is the classical presentation of a group extension 1→L→π̃→π→1: lifted relations R_α(x̃) = M_α(a), conjugation relations x̃_i a_j x̃_i^{-1} = M_ij(a), and the relations S_β(a) of L.

The groupoid setting is a morphism of groupoids p: T̃ → T, assumed surjective on π_0.
- **Generators upstairs.** One chooses a family of arrows ũ_i (i∈I) of T̃ whose projections u_i = p(ũ_i) generate T.
- **Formal inverses and words.** To handle inverses one introduces I' = I×{±1} and sets ũ'_{(i,ε)} = ũ_i^ε, and likewise u'. Words are elements of the free monoid-like set Î' = ∐_{n≥1} I'^n; the margin and the next page make this explicit.
- **Relations of the base.** Relations (4) are words u'_{i_n}…u'_{i_0} = 1 in T, made of composable arrows with or(u'_{i_0}) = ext(u'_{i_n}). They form a defining system of relations for T on the generators u_i and the object set Ob T. They play the role of the R_α.
- **Fibre arrows.** One gives arrows a_j (j∈J) of T̃ that are 'flèches fibres', i.e. p(a_j) is an identity. These are generators of the kernel groupoid K = p^{-1}(identities). With a'_{(j,±1)} = a_j^{±1}, relations (5) a'…a' = 1 define K; they play the role of the S_β.
- **Hypothesis 1°.** (4) is a defining family of relations, so Ob T consists of origins and extremities of the u_i. Since u_i = p(ũ_i), p is then surjective on objects.

The page stops before stating the conclusion. The intended statement, analogous to the Lemma, is that T̃ is presented by:
- the generators ũ_i and a_j;
- the lifted relations: each word (4) evaluated on the ũ equals a word in fibre arrows;
- the conjugation relations: ũ_i a_j ũ_i^{-1} equals a word in the a's, whenever composable;
- the relations (5).

The next page restarts the same set-up more cleanly. Purpose: to obtain presentations of Teichmüller groupoids (e.g. T_{g,ν} over T_g, or towers obtained by forgetting points or adding structure) from presentations of the base groupoid and of the fibres. This is the extension step in a generators-and-relations description of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The hypothesis 'surjective on π_0' is too weak and imprecise for the intended statement. The argument needs every object of T̃ to be connected, via kernel arrows a_j, to objects reached by the ũ_i. It also needs K = p^{-1}(identities) to be generated by the a_j as a groupoid, possibly with arrows between distinct objects of one fibre. A fibration/star-surjectivity hypothesis would be natural; the next page indeed restarts.

Conjugation relations ũ_i a_j ũ_i^{-1} only make sense when a_j sits at the source object of ũ_i. In the groupoid setting they must be indexed by composable pairs, not by all of I×J. This is not yet addressed on this page.
The conclusion of the lemma is never written down on this page; the set-up is unfinished (it is redone on p.82).

ideas.what: Presentation of a groupoid extension (morphism of groupoids with kernel of 'fibre arrows') from presentations of base and kernel: lifted relations + conjugation relations + kernel relations
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of extensions (P. Hall lemma) generalized to fibrations of groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (groups); groupoid versions in R. Brown, Higgins (groupoid theory)

ideas.what: Formalism of words as elements of ∐_{n≥1} (I×{±1})^n with composability conditions, i.e. relations in a groupoid on a set of generating arrows
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of a groupoid by generators and relations (free groupoid on a graph modulo relations)

ideas.what: Intended application: presentations of Teichmüller groupoids by induction along forgetful/extension maps (the Lego approach)
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of Teichmüller groupoid / Lego–Teichmüller game
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower and its presentation

deep.surprise_reason: Routine technical lemma: the groupoid analogue of the standard presentation of a group extension, preparatory for presenting Teichmüller groupoids. It is unfinished on this page and restarted on the next. Nothing absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Cas d'un homom. de groupoïdes' (the inserted text replaces 'groupoïde'; 'objets' is struck).
In (4) the generators are u'_{i'} with indices i^{(α)}_k ∈ I' = I×{±1}; the index tuple lies in I'^{n_α} (exponent n_α, not I'^{n_a}).
'des flèches (a_j)_{j∈J} de T̃' — the generating fibre arrows are taken in T̃ (the tilde is visible), with insertion 'flèches' replacing 'relations'.
Left margin (vertical): 'et d'où une famille de flèches ũ'_{i'} (i' ∈ I' = I×{±1}) … posant ũ'_{(i,ε)} = ũ_i^ε … et d'où une famille [de] mots, d'éléments de ∐_{n∈N*} I'^n'.
